statement: For a coefficient category A and index category I, A(I)=Fun(I^{op},A).
A functor f:I→J induces restriction f^*:A(J)→A(I) by precomposition with f^{op}.
The symbols f^?,f_!,f^*,f_*,f^! designate a successive adjunction chain in that order whenever the functors exist.
If A has all limits indexed by (f/j)^{op}, then f^* has right adjoint f_*; if A has all colimits indexed by (j/f)^{op}, it has left adjoint f_!.
repair: The pointwise formulas and the complete universal-property verification are given in the commentary at p1.

statement: Finite limits, respectively finite colimits, suffice for f_*, respectively f_!, when I and J are finite categories.
repair: The relevant comma categories have finitely many objects and arrows.
notes: Finite means a finite category, not merely finitely many objects.

statement: For A=Ab and I=(0→a,0→b), the limit functor A(I)→A has no right adjoint.
repair: The componentwise quotient (Z→[2]Z←0)→(Z/2→[0]Z/2←0) induces 0→Z/2 on limits. Hence the limit functor does not preserve epimorphisms and cannot be a left adjoint.
notes: This verifies f^! nonexistence; it is not a counterexample to existence of f_*.

statement: For A=Ab and the opposite fork, the colimit functor has no left adjoint.
repair: The componentwise injection (Z→[2]Z,Z→0)→(Q→[2]Q,Q→0) induces Z/2→0 on pushouts. Thus colimit fails to preserve monomorphisms and cannot be a right adjoint.

statement: For the open inclusion of the fork into the diamond 0→a,b→c, f_* need not have a right adjoint.
repair: Evaluation of f_* at c is the fork limit of E006, so f_* cannot preserve epimorphisms.
notes: Open means sieve in the index category.

statement: Dually, for a closed immersion, f_! need not have a left adjoint.
repair: Dualize the preceding obstruction, or use the pushout calculation of E007.

statement: If A is pointed and has the relevant limits, a closed immersion i has i_*⊣i^!.
repair: For complementary open j, form K=F×_{j_*j^*F}0. Since j^*K=0, K=i_*i^!F; its universal property proves the adjunction. Full proof in the p2 commentary.

statement: If A is pointed and has the relevant colimits, an open immersion j has j^?⊣j_!.
repair: The cofiber F∐_{i_!i^*F}0 is supported on the open; its restriction represents j^?. Full dual universal-property proof in the p2 commentary.

statement: For a fully faithful inclusion f, both existing Kan extensions f_! and f_* are fully faithful; f^* is a localization.
repair: The identity objects in the comma categories give f^*f_!≅id and f^*f_*≅id. This proves full faithfulness by the adjunction criterion.

statement: For complementary closed i:Y↪S and open j:U↪S, i_* identifies A(Y) with the full subcategory of A(S) whose restriction to U is terminal.
repair: Pointwise right Kan extension over Y/u is an empty limit when u∈U. The unit is an isomorphism for exactly the stated presheaves.

statement: Under the dual colimit hypothesis, j_! identifies A(U) with the full subcategory of A(S) whose restriction to Y is initial.
repair: The comma categories y/U are empty when y∈Y; apply the left Kan formula and the counit.

statement: When A is pointed, the natural square j_!j^*F→F, 0→i_*i^*F is both cartesian and cocartesian.
repair: Evaluate on U and on Y: in each case the square has an identity on the nonzero side. Ordinary limits and colimits of presheaves are computed pointwise.
notes: This particular square is bicartesian without stability of A.

statement: If A is abelian, 0→j_!j^*F→F→i_*i^*F→0 is exact.
repair: At each object it is one of the two split identity sequences.
notes: The sequence need not split naturally as a sequence of diagrams; the identity arrow Z→Z gives a nonsplit example.

statement: The square i_*i^!F→F, 0→j_*j^*F is cartesian, identifying i_*i^!F with the kernel of F→j_*j^*F.
gap_or_error: The sentence initially assumes only a terminal object; the edition itself supplies the necessary pointedness qualification.
repair: Use the pointed hypothesis and the pullback construction of E010; without it i^! need not exist.
notes: The editorial correction is retained in the source. It is not an AI-transcription error.

statement: If A is abelian, 0→i_*i^!F→F→j_*j^*F is exact.
repair: This is the ordinary kernel sequence from E017.
notes: No terminal zero is asserted on the right, correctly.

statement: There is a dual cocartesian support square under the relevant pointed colimit hypotheses.
gap_or_error: The short wording recalls initial objects but does not repeat pointedness.
repair: Read the dual of the corrected assertion E017: use the cofiber of i_!i^*F→F and j_!j^?F.

statement: For a monotone map of finite ordinals, restriction on A-valued presheaves has a second adjoint on each side when A is pointed and has finite limits and colimits.
repair: Proved here by factoring the map into elementary faces and degeneracies and using the explicit extended adjunction chain.
notes: The tentative assertion is true with the standing relevant-(co)limit assumption; pointedness by itself need not provide kernels and cokernels.

statement: All restriction functors associated with all maps between two fixed finite ordinals occur in the same successive adjunction chain.
gap_or_error: The edition already rejects this generalization.
repair: For the pair [1],[1], identity restriction has only identity adjoints up to isomorphism, whereas constant-map restriction is not identity for A=Ab.
notes: The manuscript presents it tentatively; the editorial counterindication is correct.

statement: For [n] and [n+1], the face and degeneracy restrictions form a chain of 2n+3 terms, extendible by two terms at each end to 2n+7.
gap_or_error: This counts the injective faces and surjective degeneracies, not every monotone map between the two ordinals.
repair: The p3 commentary proves the chain δ^{n+1*}⊣σ^{n*}⊣δ^{n*}⊣⋯⊣σ^{0*}⊣δ^{0*} and constructs its four endpoints.
notes: The printed count is correct after the editors’ restriction; the stated verification for n=0,1 is extended by the proof.

statement: Dia is a full 2-subcategory of small categories, used as the domain of index shapes.
notes: Size universes are implicit in the manuscript; the commentary uses small index categories.

statement: A category in which every arrow is monic and every isomorphism is an identity is a poset.
gap_or_error: The criterion does not force Hom sets to have at most one element.
repair: Replace it by thin and skeletal. The parallel-pair category has only monomorphisms and identity isomorphisms but is not thin.
notes: Already corrected in the edition, whose counterexample is valid.

statement: The index domain must satisfy closure conditions, at least finite products and binary coproducts, and further closure conditions for later constructions.
repair: The later comma-category and opposite constructions require the corresponding shapes to remain in Dia.
notes: No final list of domain axioms is claimed here.

statement: A preliminary prederivator is a strict 2-functor Dia^{coop}→CAT, reversing both functors and natural transformations.
notes: The text calls it a derivator subject to further conditions and writes Dia^∘. This is the presheaf convention, distinct from the modern covariant-diagram Cat^{op} convention.

statement: For I→[f]J→[g]K, the restrictions satisfy (gf)^*=f^*g^* strictly.
notes: Part of strict 2-functoriality.

statement: A natural transformation α:f⇒g induces α^*:g^*⇒f^*.
repair: For a represented example its i-component is F(α_i):F(g(i))→F(f(i)).

statement: For composable transformations α,β, (βα)^*=α^*β^*, and identities of index functors and transformations are sent to identities.
notes: Horizontal composition compatibility is included in the term strict 2-functor, even though not separately displayed.

statement: Preliminary Der_1 requires both adjoints f_!⊣f^*⊣f_* for each allowed index functor.
notes: This is not the final Der 1 numbering used later in this chapter.

statement: A preliminary left derivator requires all f_* and f_! for open immersions.
notes: The name refers to left exactness/right Kan extensions, as in the presheaf convention.

statement: A preliminary right derivator requires all f_! and f_* for closed immersions.
Preliminary Der_2 requires i_*⊣i^! for a closed immersion in the pointed situation.
gap_or_error: Without pointedness this excludes HOT; the author’s footnote explicitly removes that requirement.
repair: Keep the pointed qualification. In the modern complete derivator axioms this extra adjoint follows from pointedness.

statement: Preliminary Der_2 dually requires j^?⊣j_! for an open immersion in the pointed situation.
repair: Apply the dual of the pointed construction.

statement: For open or closed immersions restriction is required to be a localization; equivalently its existing left or right Kan adjoint is fully faithful.
notes: The equivalence is the usual unit/counit criterion for a reflective or coreflective localization.

statement: The essential image of closed i_* consists of coefficients terminal on the open complement, and the essential image of open j_! consists of coefficients initial on the closed complement.
notes: Added in footnote 3; later it follows from the pointwise Kan formulas.

statement: In the one-sided left theory only closed exceptional right inverse images are required; in the right theory only open exceptional left inverse images are required.
notes: Subject throughout to pointedness for exceptional adjoints.

statement: A pointed prederivator has pointed coefficient categories D(I), with restrictions preserving zero objects.
notes: The later full derivator axioms allow pointedness to be checked at e alone.

statement: Preliminary Der_2′ requires D(I∐J)→D(I)×D(J) induced by restrictions to be an equivalence.
notes: The displayed ∼ is read as equivalence of categories; no empty-shape condition is stated in this preliminary formulation.

statement: Every prederivator has the partial underlying-diagram functor D(I×J)→Fun(J^{op},D(I)).
repair: Compose J→Fun(I,I×J) with the contravariant action on Hom categories and curry. The text gives this construction.
notes: The resulting diagram has shape J^{op}, not J.

statement: Given an incoherent diagram K→D(I), ask whether it comes canonically from a coefficient in D(I×K^{op}).
gap_or_error: This is a programmatic lifting question, not a universal lifting axiom.
repair: For arrow shapes strongness supplies existence and fullness, not a preferred or unique lift. Specific support squares are constructed using their extra adjunction data.
notes: We do not label this unqualified question an open conjecture.

statement: The support square of p8 should arise functorially from a coherent object over I×[1]×[1].
repair: In the pointed theory the restriction, zero-extension, and adjunction constructions give the needed coherent support square.
notes: The text has not yet supplied the completed axioms or the construction.

statement: A coherent cartesian square is a right Kan extension from the cospan corner W×I, with W=[1]^2−{(1,1)}.
notes: Presheaf variance makes W^{op} a cospan. This is a homotopy-cartesian condition, not an ordinary categorical pullback in D(I).

statement: The cartesian and cocartesian constructions of the first support square should be canonically isomorphic.
repair: Both constructions give the same coherent support square, whose cartesian and cocartesian conditions are checked pointwise on U and Y.
notes: This special bicartesian square does not assert that every cartesian square is cocartesian.

statement: The fundamental or base category is A_D=D(e); its objects are fundamental coefficients.
There is a canonical underlying-diagram functor D(I)→Fun(I^{op},D(e)), F↦(i↦i^*F).
gap_or_error: The supplied TeX incorrectly attaches the vertical equality in the displayed diagram to the whole Hom category.
repair: Attach D(e) only to the coefficient symbol A, as in the PDF.
notes: This is a transcription/layout error; the mathematical statement of the source is correct.

statement: Preliminary Der_3 requires the underlying-diagram functor to be conservative: a coherent map is invertible exactly when every evaluation is invertible.
The underlying-diagram functor need not be faithful.
repair: The nonsplit extension 0→(0→Z)→(Z→[1]Z)→(Z→0)→0 yields a nonzero derived morphism with both evaluations zero. Full example in commentary at p11.
notes: Conservativity does not imply faithfulness.

statement: Under preliminary Der_3, D(I×J)→Fun(J^{op},D(I)) is conservative.
repair: If the J-components are isomorphisms, every (i,j)-component is an isomorphism; apply Der_3 to I×J.
notes: The text’s displayed F_(i,j)≅θ(F)(j)_i is a complete proof.

statement: A coherent coefficient over I refines its underlying I^{op}-diagram by additional global information.
notes: Interpretive statement substantiated by E048; not an assertion that a particular extra structure on every incoherent diagram has been classified.

statement: A model presentation begins with a category M and a class W of selected arrows, and base category M[W^{-1}].
notes: The quotation marks around model category matter: this initial datum is a relative category, not yet a Quillen structure.

statement: For M_I=Fun(I^{op},M), W_I consists of natural transformations whose every component lies in W.
The associated coefficient category is D_(M,W)(I)=M_I[W_I^{-1}].
notes: Existence as a locally small category is a size issue not automatic for an arbitrary relative category.

statement: The localized diagram construction is contravariantly 2-functorial in I.
repair: Restriction preserves W_I, and all natural transformations descend through localization. A functorial localization gives strictness; arbitrary choices give equivalent coherent data.
notes: No Quillen structure is needed for this formal assertion, aside from the localization/size issue.

statement: A Quillen model category gives derived left and right Kan extensions and hence a derivator when the relevant small (co)limits exist.
gap_or_error: The manuscript attributes the result to Thomason but gives no precise bibliographical identification.
repair: Cisinski proves the right-Kan/left-derivator statement for a model category with small limits; dualize for left Kan extensions.
notes: The theorem is established; the exact historical Thomason attribution remains unverified.

statement: Is M_I itself a Quillen model category with the objectwise weak equivalences, perhaps with fibrations and cofibrations specified objectwise?
gap_or_error: No unconditional simultaneous objectwise prescription is valid.
repair: For combinatorial M, projective and injective structures exist; projective fibrations and injective cofibrations are objectwise. General Kan existence does not require such structures. More flexible model notions are stable under arbitrary presheaves.
references: Groth2013, Theorem 1.28 and Proposition 1.30; Cisinski2010, Theorem 6.22 and Corollary 6.24
notes: This is a question, not an erroneous assertion that both classes can be objectwise.

statement: HOT is the derivator associated with simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences; its base is the ordinary homotopy category of spaces.
notes: The source’s semi-simplicial terminology includes degeneracy maps, as shown by the full simplex category Δ.

statement: (sSet)^{I^{op}}≅Set^{Δ^{op}×I^{op}}≅(Set^{I^{op}})^{Δ^{op}}.
repair: This is the ordinary exponential law for functor categories.
notes: Weak equivalences are objectwise in I, not unspecified local equivalences of a site.

statement: A preliminary strict morphism u:D→D′ consists of component functors u_I commuting with restrictions and their natural transformations.
notes: The parenthetical strict? points toward the modern use of pseudonatural morphisms with coherent invertible structure cells.

statement: Commutation on the objects of Fun(I,J) does not by itself impose the required commutation on its arrows; square (2) includes the latter requirement.
repair: This is the natural-transformation compatibility in the definition of a 2-natural morphism, which the text explicitly spells out.

statement: A weak-equivalence-preserving functor (M,W)→(M′,W′) induces a morphism of the associated localized prederivators.
repair: Apply the functor objectwise. It commutes with restriction before localization, and preserves all selected objectwise arrows.
notes: Footnote 5 asks for this example; preservation of Kan extensions is additional.

statement: A morphism is called left exact, respectively right exact, when it commutes via canonical mates with all relevant f_*, respectively f_!; exact means both.
notes: This preliminary terminology uses all relevant Kan extensions, stronger than modern finite exactness for stable derivators.

statement: HOTAB has base category D^{≤0}(Ab), the full derived subcategory of complexes with cohomology zero in positive degrees.
notes: It is connective and pointed, not the unbounded stable derived theory.

statement: Simplicial abelian groups, localized at quasi-isomorphisms, present HOTAB.
repair: Normalization gives the Dold–Kan equivalence with nonnegative chain complexes, which sends weak equivalences to quasi-isomorphisms.

statement: The free abelianization functor from spaces to connective derived abelian groups extends to a morphism HOT→HOTAB.
repair: Use degreewise free abelian group on all diagram categories. It preserves weak equivalences and defines a derived left Quillen morphism.

statement: The abelianization morphism preserves all right Kan extensions.
gap_or_error: Its preservation is questioned in the body and rejected in footnote 7.
repair: It already fails to preserve the terminal object: Z[*]=Z≠0. The explicit finite pullback calculation in the commentary gives Z^4→Z^3.
notes: The negative answer is part of the source itself, not a newly discovered error.

statement: A homotopy pullback of spaces along a fibration is sent by abelianization to a homotopy pullback.
gap_or_error: The source footnote supplies the negative correction.
repair: Take X=Y′={0,1}, Y=*. The four-point pullback maps to Z^4; the pullback of the two augmentations Z^2→Z is Z^3. The comparison has kernel generated by e00−e01−e10+e11.

statement: Abelianization sends homotopy pushouts of spaces to homotopy pushouts in HOTAB.
repair: The free simplicial abelian group functor is a left Quillen adjoint, so its derived morphism preserves homotopy colimits. This answers the dual question positively.
notes: It must be separated from the false pullback assertion.

statement: A morphism u:D→D′ has canonical right-Kan mate u_J f_*^D→f_*^{D′}u_I.
repair: The p14 commentary writes the full composite of the target unit, the restriction comparison, and the source counit.

statement: A morphism u:D→D′ has canonical left-Kan mate f_!^{D′}u_I→u_J f_!^D.
repair: Transpose u_I→u_I f_D^* f_!^D→f_{D′}^*u_J f_!^D under the target adjunction. The comparison orientation in the text is correct.

statement: Analogous comparison and preservation questions arise for exceptional inverse images along closed or open immersions.
repair: Mate the corresponding adjunction diagrams; invertibility requires additional preservation assumptions and does not follow merely from a morphism of prederivators.

statement: One may consider morphisms that preserve only left, only right, or both kinds of homotopy Kan extension.
notes: Footnote 9 appropriately corrects the body’s initial inclination to require both for every morphism. Modern morphisms need neither unless explicitly stipulated.

statement: In the stable/triangulated setting, finite homotopy-limit and finite homotopy-colimit exactness coincide.
gap_or_error: The footnote is correct for finite exactness, but must not be interpreted as equating arbitrary Kan-extension preservation.
repair: Restrict to finite exactness; tensor with Q on D(Z) preserves coproducts and finite exact structure but not products.
notes: This qualifies the interpretation rather than declaring the finite statement false.

statement: What model-level exactness and weak-equivalence/fibration/cofibration compatibility suffice to construct exact morphisms of derivators?
repair: Right Quillen adjoints induce derived morphisms preserving homotopy limits; left Quillen adjoints give the dual statement. This is sufficient, not asserted necessary.

statement: DER denotes the 2-category of derivators.
notes: One must specify the chosen morphisms and modifications; the manuscript is still settling the exactness convention.

statement: The dual prederivator is D^∘(I)=D(I^{op})^{op}.
notes: Requires closure of the index domain under opposites.

statement: The action on Hom categories for the dual is obtained by applying opposite-category duality to the original 2-functor.
gap_or_error: The displayed identification initially gives indices (I^{op},J^{op}) rather than (I,J); the edition explicitly corrects them.
repair: Use D^∘_{I^{op},J^{op}} at the indicated point, or relabel I,J throughout.
notes: The source’s proof is otherwise formal and complete.

statement: If D is presented by (M,W), then D^∘ is presented by (M^{op},W^{op}).
repair: Fun(I^{op},M^{op})≅Fun(I,M)^{op}, and localization commutes with opposites by its universal property.

statement: Given a base-category functor u_0:D(e)→D′(e), ask whether it extends to a morphism of derivators.
gap_or_error: The sentence is methodological and does not provide sufficient hypotheses for existence or uniqueness.
repair: In examples constructed from model or higher-categorical functors, the coherent lift provides the answer; no automatic extension theorem follows from the base functor alone.
notes: Do not promote the phrase in practice into a general existence theorem.

statement: In the intended examples the coherent extension is canonically determined up to canonical isomorphism.
gap_or_error: This is a description of constructions available in practice, not a formally quantified uniqueness theorem.
repair: Specify the model-level functor or coherent universal property when claiming uniqueness.

statement: Is evaluation Hom(D,D′)→Hom(D(e),D′(e)) fully faithful? The author doubts this in general.
gap_or_error: No proof or precise domain/morphism hypotheses are supplied here.
repair: For unrestricted morphisms the p18 commentary proves that evaluation is not faithful: use the represented derivator of [1] and a nonzero derived-arrow morphism with zero components. It induces a nonzero modification whose e-component vanishes.
references: Groth2013, Examples 1.2(1) and 1.6 (represented construction and bicompleteness criterion)
notes: The explicit argument also works for strict natural morphisms. It does not address additional requirements that every morphism preserve all Kan extensions; no open-modern-conjecture claim is made.

statement: The shifted prederivator D_I is defined by D_I(J)=D(I×J).
notes: The canonical identification I×e≅I makes D(I) its base category, up to the standard product identification.

statement: The shift acts on index functors and transformations by product with id_I, followed by D; thus f^*_{D_I}=(id_I×f)^*_D.
Existence of the applicable Kan adjoints and iterated adjoints is inherited by the shift.
repair: Apply the original existence axiom to id_I×f. Products preserve the required open or closed immersion conditions.

statement: Preliminary Der_2, including the support image conditions, is inherited by shifts.
repair: Products with I preserve complementary sieves/cosieves, and the corresponding essential images are expressed by vanishing or terminal restrictions to the product complement.

statement: Preliminary Der_3 is inherited by shifts.
repair: If every J-evaluation is invertible in D(I), all (i,j)-evaluations are invertible; use Der_3 for D(I×J).

statement: Every additional derivator axiom must be checked for stability under shifts.
repair: The full pointwise-Kan axiom is subsequently covered by the shift theorem.
notes: A methodological requirement, not an omitted proof of an axiom already stated.

statement: For f:I→I′, restriction lifts to the morphism D_{I′}→D_I with J-component (f×id_J)^*.
repair: Products in the two separate variables commute, and strict 2-functoriality supplies the restriction coherence.

statement: The components (f×id_J)_! and (f×id_J)_* define the corresponding Kan-extension morphisms D_I→D_{I′}.
gap_or_error: Writing components alone does not prove their pseudonaturality.
repair: Verify invertibility of the product base-change mates and their pasting coherence; these are established by the later pointwise Kan axioms.
notes: The following manuscript pages investigate exactly these comparisons.

statement: I↦D_I is functorial contravariantly via restrictions and covariantly via each available Kan extension.
repair: Restriction is strict; the adjoint variants are pseudofunctorial via the canonical composition isomorphisms and their coherence.
notes: Do not read functorial here as strict equality for arbitrary independent choices of adjoints.

statement: Existing exceptional inverse images along the relevant immersions likewise lift to morphisms between shifted derivators.
repair: Use their coherent pointed support constructions or the parameterwise mate argument.

statement: Do restriction, Kan extensions, and exceptional inverse images between shifts commute with all left and right Kan extensions in the other variable?
gap_or_error: The answer is not uniformly affirmative: like-variance Kan extensions commute, whereas arbitrary mixed homotopy limits and colimits need not.
repair: The product base-change axiom gives continuity and cocontinuity of restrictions; Fubini gives same-variance commutation; mixed commutation requires further hypotheses.
notes: This is taken up explicitly on manuscript pp23–25, outside this fragment.

statement: The square with sides $f\times1_J$, $1_I\times g$, $f\times1_{J'}$ and $1_{I'}\times g$ is a categorical pullback.
repair: Immediate from the universal property of the product.

statement: Restriction $f^*:\mathbb D_{I'}\to\mathbb D_I$ commutes with right Kan extensions in the independent variable, once the pointwise derivator axioms hold.
repair: Use pointwise Kan formulas and final-object contraction in the unused slice; equivalently base change for projections.

statement: By duality the same restriction morphism commutes with left Kan extensions; it is continuous and cocontinuous.
repair: Dual of the preceding claim.
notes: The manuscript first swaps left/right exactness; the edition already supplies the bracketed correction.

statement: The morphism $f_*:\mathbb D_I\to\mathbb D_{I'}$ commutes with right Kan extensions in another variable.
repair: Both composites are right adjoints to the same restriction; uniqueness of adjoints gives the canonical interchange isomorphism.

statement: Dually $f_!$ commutes with left Kan extensions in an independent variable.

statement: There is a canonical mixed interchange map $G'_!F_*\to F'_*G_!$.
repair: The displayed construction is the mate of $F_*\to F_*G^*G_!\cong {G'}^*F'_*G_!$.

statement: The mixed interchange map might be invertible in additive derivators.

statement: If every $f_*$ commutes with every independent left Kan extension, every $g_!$ commutes with every independent right Kan extension.
repair: The two formulations assert invertibility of the same mixed interchange map with the two variables relabelled.

statement: For a non-surjective closed inclusion in set-valued presheaves, $f_*$ does not preserve the initial object.
repair: It extends by a singleton outside the inclusion; the initial presheaf has empty fibres.

statement: Under the cohomological derivator axioms, every $\mathbb D(I)$ has finite categorical products.

repair: The diagonal has a right adjoint. Apply Der1 to $I\times S$ for finite discrete $S$ and Der3 to the projection.

statement: Under the homological derivator axioms, every $\mathbb D(I)$ has finite categorical coproducts.

statement: A morphism commuting with all right (respectively left) Kan extensions preserves the finite products (respectively coproducts) in every value; in particular it preserves final (respectively initial) objects.

statement: For a category $\mathcal M$, the represented prederivator is $\mathbb D_{\mathcal M}(I)=\operatorname{Fun}(I^{op},\mathcal M)$; localizing at the empty class changes nothing.

statement: The shift of a represented prederivator satisfies $(\mathbb D_{\mathcal M})_I\simeq\mathbb D_{\operatorname{Fun}(I^{op},\mathcal M)}$.

statement: The assignment $\mathcal M\mapsto\mathbb D_{\mathcal M}$ is locally an equivalence: $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M,\mathcal M')\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb D_{\mathcal M},\mathbb D_{\mathcal M'})$.
repair: Evaluation at the point is inverse to postcomposition, up to the pseudonaturality isomorphisms; naturality at the walking arrow determines diagram arrows and modifications.

gap_or_error: Ordinary finite left exactness is insufficient if the diagram domain contains infinite shapes and the manuscript exactness means all Kan extensions.

statement: For a represented prederivator, asking $f_*^{\mathbb D}$ to commute with all left Kan extensions is equivalent to asking its base functor $\mathcal M(I)\to\mathcal M(I')$ to preserve the corresponding colimits.
repair: Apply the preceding represented-morphism statement and the exponential law.

statement: For $I=[1]^2\setminus\{(1,1)\}$, right Kan extension of a presheaf along $I\hookrightarrow[1]^2$ fills the missing corner by $F_a\times_{F_0}F_b$.
repair: The slice at the missing final object is the entire cospan indexing the pullback.

statement: In an abelian coefficient category the missing value is $K(F)=\ker(F_a\oplus F_b\xrightarrow{\alpha-\beta}F_0)$.
repair: The kernel universal property equals the pullback universal property.

statement: The pointwise epimorphism $F\to F'$ which replaces $F_0$ by zero induces $K(F)\hookrightarrow F_a\oplus F_b$; this is epic exactly when both structure maps vanish.
repair: The kernel inclusion is epic iff it is an isomorphism, iff $\alpha-\beta=0$; restrict to each summand.

statement: There should be a stable or triangulated derivator theory in which left and right exact morphisms coincide.
gap_or_error: Correct for finite exactness, false for the earlier all-Kan-extension meaning.
repair: Stable derivators: preservation of final objects and cartesian squares is equivalent to preservation of initial objects and cocartesian squares. Infinite products and coproducts need not commute.

notes: The question is settled with the stated finiteness qualification; not open.

statement: For $f:I\to J$ and $j\in J$, $I/j=(f/j)$ has objects $(i,\varphi:f(i)\to j)$ and projection $q:I/j\to I$.
